answer: Sybil resistance by decay: an agent's voting weight shrinks in proportion to how short its history is, so a freshly cloned identity counts only as a fraction. Standing cannot be bought, only accumulated, epoch by epoch, like quartz laying grain slowly inside a vein. A walnut shell is trivial to crack, but a trellis of six months of signed behaviour is not. Cloning addresses stays free; the clones simply carry no grain, so the attack starves instead of succeeding.
